answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and no auto-renew, and the line already running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any action that introduces transition risk (switching vendors, or deferring past expiration) directly threatens delivery continuity — the explicit hard constraint alongside TCO. Negotiate_terms is foreclosed this cycle since the incumbent already refused to reopen price. Switch_primary_vendor (memory_c2) offers cost upside but was learned under different capacity conditions with slack to absorb onboarding friction; attempting it now, at 94% utilization with no buffer, risks a delivery interruption the business cannot absorb. Defer_decision is even riskier given the contract does not auto-renew — deferral could leave supply uncovered entirely. Renew_incumbent (memory_c1) is the only option that preserves continuity and avoids migration risk during a period with no slack, even though it does not satisfy the 18% cost mandate this cycle. I verified memory_c1 specifically because it underpins the safety case for the action I'm committing to under time pressure. The unmet cost-cut mandate and the cost-vs-risk tradeoff on switching vendors should be explicitly carried into next cycle's review rather than treated as resolved.
